$comment: Generated by tools/harness/makingof.mjs. One entry per archived image, oldest first.

entries.caption: First pixels: the M0 bootstrap scene (banded island, four tribe totems, Preact title) captured headless on the RTX GPU
Same scene through the software SwiftShader path, used by the doctor to pick the GPU screenshot mode
First Gemini concept reference image (smoke call), before the style direction is chosen
First generated 3D asset: Meshy low-poly tree after the Blender normalize pass (322 tris)
A0 asset QA contact sheet: first tree model and first concept image
Soft pastel toy diorama: candidate art direction 1 of 6
Bold saturated papercraft: candidate art direction 2 of 6
Matte clay miniature: candidate art direction 3 of 6
Crisp flat-shaded polygon: candidate art direction 4 of 6
Warm painterly low-poly: candidate art direction 5 of 6

Tilt-shift tabletop miniature: candidate art direction 6 of 6. Not picked on day one, but on 10/09 Stewart called it his favorite (trees, thatched huts, water, the tilt-shift view), so it became the second reference and BACKLOG 14a
The six candidate art directions generated in A1, before the pick
The chosen art direction: crisp flat-shaded polygon (ref_04), lit with the warm golden-hour haze of ref_05
Gemini concept of the Settler (humble villager, azure waist band) generated with the chosen ref_04 faceted low-poly style as reference, input to the Meshy image-to-3D bake-off route.
Gemini concept of the Warden (club, round hide shield, azure sash) in the chosen faceted low-poly style, input to the Meshy image-to-3D bake-off route.
Unit bake-off: Settler and Warden built two ways in Meshy meshy-t2, text-to-3D preview (route A) beside Gemini concept to image-to-3D (route B), with the two concepts below.
Unit bake-off re-rendered with vertex colors visible: text-to-3D untextured versus image-to-3D textured for Settler and Warden.
First renderer contact sheet: faceted torus planet with curved horizon, wrap seam, globe zoom, map view, islands and a raised cone
Overview: placeholder pines and broadleaf trees on banded terrain with shoreline foam
Globe zoom: the 128 cell torus reads as a small round planet thanks to the curved-world bend
All eleven village buildings as textured image-to-3D models snapped to the palette, each next to its Gemini concept, with a blue tribe banner region.
Three trees and three rocks from untextured text-to-3D previews, colored by height and facing with the palette.
Gemini concept for the village hearth: stacked stones around an ember bowl with a blue banner pole.
Gemini concept for the small round thatched dwelling in the ref_04 low-poly style.
Gemini concept for the fire lodge with a glowing doorway and clay chimney.
People appear: the Shaper with her staff, five azure settlers around the Hearth fire, wild people wandering nearby
Box-selected settlers with selection rings walking to a right-click target on the curved surface
The six v1 tribe units as game models beside their Gemini concepts: shaper, settler, warden, firecaller, chanter and wild person, each about 1400 tris with azure cloth regions.
Concept art for the Shaper: a tall robed caster with a feathered horned headdress and a carved staff topped with a glowing stone.
A village grows: the first dwelling built by settlers, HUD v1 with population, mana income, split slider and spell charges
Spell, resource, building and unit icons: Gemini emblems in the ref_04 low-poly style keyed from magenta, plus the Blender thumbnails on transparent backgrounds.
Seven spell VFX textures keyed from pure black and shown additively over terrain green: bolt burst, lightning, hornets, lava, magic ring, dust, water.
The Shaper's power: all eight v1 spells captured just after they resolve
Volcano: a cone rises, lava pools burn and molten rocks scatter
Raise Land bridges a deep channel from the Shaper toward her target
Stewart's pick and the art target: dense 16-bit village on a small planet in space, terraced cliffs, foamy turquoise sea, stone-framed HUD
Retro pixel candidate 2: HD-2D pixel sprites in a tilt-shift 3D diorama
Technique reference: stylized low-poly 3D with pixel-textured surfaces, dusk light and pixel fire
Retro pixel candidate 4: flat 16-bit pixel art with an atmospheric planet rim
Retro pixel candidate 5: late-90s PC strategy look with a stone and wood spell bar
Retro pixel candidate 6: flat-shaded low-poly with dithered pixel shading and crisp outlines
Retro pixel candidate 7: bright modern pixel art with a cozy palette
First retro render pass (ADR-005): chunky pixels, dithered palette, firelit Hearth and a stone and wood HUD, the first step toward Stewart's pick
Look v2: retro pass v1 (left), space sky, turquoise sea with foam strokes, brown cliffs, steep curved camera and HUD layout v2 (middle), Stewart's target (right)
Look v2 overview: the home island on a small planet in space
Look v2 globe zoom: the world as a planet among the stars
M6 combat: a Firecaller's fireball arcs onto four settlers
M6 combat VFX shots: fireball, chant, melee
M6 HUD troop panel: stances and retreat for six selected units, lodges in the build column
First raid: the aggressive opponent AI's warden wave reaches an idle player's Hearth at minute 9 and has already killed the Shaper (back in 30 s)
M7 ai shot set contact sheet (review only, not in npm run qa)
M8 game flow: main menu, skirmish setup, settings with rebindable keys, pause, save slots and the victory screen, from the e2e run at 1280x720.
M8 HUD v2: objectives panel, spell charge ETAs, selected unit chips, and the minimap camera footprint with Shaper markers.
The Hearthfall main menu at 1440p over a slowly turning planet.
M9 campaign: level select (levels open in order), the first teaching level, the level-won screen, and placeholder shrines (a rival tribe in red praying at the contested hill shrine)
The Contested Shrine: the rival tribe reaches the hill shrine first and its prayers tint the orb red
The Contested Shrine after the M9 review: the hill shrine moved closer to the Hearth so a late start can still win
Campaign shrines and the Hearth as real models (M10 levels set)
Before and after: placeholder meshes give way to the real Hearth and follower models
M10 exit: the smoke set with every placeholder swapped for the generated models
Before M11: chant pulse washed out to white, crimson units stand on nothing, the Shaper the same size as her followers
After M11: violet chant halo, tribe rings under every unit, a larger Shaper on a larger ring
M11 close view of a starting village: tribe rings, the Hearth model and real settler models in the retro pass
M11 combat contact sheet: fireball glow trail, violet chant halo, melee dust, tribe rings
BACKLOG 1: the eight later spells in play (Veil, Ward, Beguile, Whirlwind, Mire, Erode, Firerain, Wraith) and the 16-slot spell bar
BACKLOG 1: icon sheet with the eight new spell icons beside the M10 set
BACKLOG 0a: a village before (left) and after (right): building models at 1.3x, tall conifers and the grove ring around the Hearth
BACKLOG 0a: terraced plateaus, level bands and cliff steps from the generator
BACKLOG 0a: the volcano now throws a dark ash column with embers at the vent
BACKLOG 0c: stone arrives. A grey outcrop stands in a clearing near the first Dwelling; settlers quarry it for towers and lodges, and it shrinks as they do.
Shade unit: Gemini concept beside the normalized Meshy model thumbnail (hooded charcoal cloak, azure sash)
Shade Den lodge: Gemini concept beside the normalized Meshy model thumbnail (low dark hut, hanging cloth)
BACKLOG 3: fog of war. The home island in sight, the rest of the planet dark until scouted.
Hero shot of the current build: the Shaper and five followers at the Hearth, real models in the retro pixel pass, the ground beyond the village going dark under the new fog of war.

BACKLOG 4 added formations: a mixed group ordered across the field settles into a box, Wardens with clubs in front, settlers in the middle, Firecallers, the Chanter and the Shaper behind, instead of crowding one point. Also new: double-click type select, control group camera jump, spell preview counts and an undo countdown

BACKLOG 5 added unit animation: the pose gallery plays every clip side by side (Wardens above, settlers below): walk with swinging legs, chop, club swing, throw, cast with both arms up, kneel and pray, panic, idle breathing. Units that die now topple over, and drowned ones flail and sink

BACKLOG 6, difficulty levels: each level fought a normal opponent of the same personality for 20 minutes on 8 seeds. Easy was retuned (slower reactions, 0.7x income) and now wins 1 of 8, while hard and brutal win 7 of 8. Brutal's 1.25x income goes through the sim as a visible handicap command, not hidden AI code.

BACKLOG 8 accessibility. Added: a colorblind tribe palette (deep blue, orange, purple, mint), chosen by simulating red-green and blue-yellow color blindness so every pair of tribes stays far apart for every viewer; here at 125 percent HUD scale on 1920x1080. Also added: subtitles for Shaper barks and a UI scale setting.

BACKLOG 8: the first 125 percent HUD on a 1280x720 window put the stats panel over the spell bar and the build column over the minimap. Changed: the HUD now shrinks itself in 5 percent steps until nothing overlaps (150 percent asked, about 105 fits here).
Look v3 tilt-shift test: off, pre and post the palette pass at pixel sizes 3 and 2, plus the close camera; post chosen (ADR-013).
Foreground crop, left to right: no tilt-shift, post (smooth lens blur, the pick) and pre (blur re-dithered into grain).
Look v3, painted water: depth sampled per pixel from a heightmap texture gives smooth turquoise shallows, a crisp shore foam line and a faint wave ring drifting offshore.
Look v3, trees: round clumped broadleaves in yellow-greens fill the lowlands while conifers keep the heights, each grove jittered warm or cool.
Look v3 dwellings: the old conical huts (top) against the new thatched round huts with cream walls and roof pennants (bottom), made for about one dollar.
The thatched huts in game beside the Hearth, under the miniature focus band.
Look v3 terrain: snow caps on the high peaks and terraced cliffs.
Lighting presets and weather: day, golden (default) and evening, plus rain with streaks and a dimmer, greyer light; the unlit water follows the preset.
Before and after look v3: the same close and overview cameras from run 1 and after stretch 2 block A (tilt-shift miniature focus, painted water, clumped trees, golden light).
Stretch 2 polish: the main menu gets a title illustration cropped from the miniature concept art that set the look v3 direction
Quake lead-in: the ground cracks and a dark edge marks the danger zone for 1.5 s, then the land drops, so players can see the cause before units drown
Stretch 2 block D: the skirmish setup picks a victory rule (Conquest, Hold the Reliquaries, King of the Hill, Last Stand), now decided inside the deterministic sim
Stretch 2 block E: the campaign becomes a route map of seven levels; spells a Reliquary teaches now carry into later levels
Worship readability: a ring around the Reliquary fills in the praying tribe's color, and the objective shows the prayer percent
Boats: five settlers and wardens ride a longboat across a strait they could never walk; the sail wears the tribe color
Balloons: a hide balloon carries a Firecaller over the water and lets it shoot from the basket; the ring below marks where it flies
The Boathouse must stand by the water and launches a boat every 45 seconds

Forge mode (BACKLOG 11): before the match your people stand still while you reshape the land around your Hearth. The white ring is where the brush may land, the yellow circle the brush itself; the panel counts down 2 minutes and 120 strokes, with Raise, Lower, Flatten, Smooth and Ready.
Forge mode: the turtle AI spends its two free minutes digging a moat around its Hearth, leaving gaps toward and away from its rival
Campaign level 12, The Forge: two minutes before battle, the rival digs its moat while the player's strokes wait
Campaign level 9, The Sky Road: a Reliquary on a sea stack that only a balloon can reach
The campaign route grows to 13 levels: boats, balloons, both new victory types, a Forge level and a three-island finale
The map editor: paint sea and hills, drop Hearths, Reliquaries and trees on a live preview planet, pick a goal, then Playtest
Map view before BACKLOG 37/40: a perspective camera high above, so the map bulges and its edges follow ragged chunk boundaries
Map view after BACKLOG 37/40: an orthographic camera fitted to the window, straight edges, a dark frame past the world edge and a light grid
Replay viewer: every finished match can be watched again, scrubbed, sped up to 8x and checked against its recorded hash
Records and achievements: career stats counted from the event log and 15 achievements defined as data
Localization scaffold: the pseudo locale pads and accents every migrated string so layout checks catch text that would not fit a longer language

BACKLOG 48: economy bots on islands 128 with 4 tribes for 20 minutes. Before the fixes three of six seeds stalled (a plan on an unreachable pocket froze every job; one stranded settler kept the rest from moving home). Now all six are clean; the one flat line is a tribe whose island is full.
BACKLOG 39: close-up ground detail, grass tufts, flowers and pebbles near the camera
First match tips (stretch 2 playtest pass): a new player's first skirmish walks through Dwelling, Bolt, lodge, troops and attack-move, one tip at a time under the spell bar.
